# `silk/option`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Optional owned values that are present or absent, with no explanation for the absence.

## When to use
Use [`Option`](#Option) when "no value" is a normal answer, such as a lookup that finds nothing. Use
`silk.result.Result` when the caller must know why the value is missing.

Use [`map`](#Option.impl.map) to transform a present value, [`flatMap`](#Option.impl.flatMap) when the next step can also produce no
value, and [`unwrapOr`](#Option.impl.unwrapOr) to get a plain value with a fallback. Use `match` when the present and
absent cases need different custom behavior.

## Details
`Option<T>` is a union with the variants [`Some`](#Option.Some) and [`None`](#Option.None). Each combinator consumes the
option. A present value moves into the result. A value that the operation does not use is
dropped. No combinator copies `T`, so `T` does not need to be `Copy`.

## Examples
### Look up a port and fall back to a default
```silk
import silk.option { Option }

fn portFor(scheme: string) -> Option<i32> {
  if scheme == "http" {
    return Option<i32>.some(80)
  }
  return Option<i32>.none()
}

fn secure(port: i32) -> Option<i32> {
  if port == 80 {
    return Option<i32>.some(443)
  }
  return Option<i32>.none()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let known = portFor("http") |> Option<i32>.flatMap<i32>(secure) |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(8080)
  let unknown = portFor("gopher") |> Option<i32>.flatMap<i32>(secure) |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(8080)
  if known != 443 || unknown != 8080 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Make a service optional
An effect that requires `&Option<&S>` runs with or without a provider of `S`. See [`withSome`](#withSome).
```silk
import silk.effect { Effect }
import silk.option { Option, provideSome, withSome }

service Tracer {
  effect fn trace(value: i32) -> i32 ? &Tracer
}

struct Offset {
  amount: i32,
}

impl Tracer for Offset {
  effect fn trace(self: &Self, value: i32) -> i32 {
    return value + self.amount
  }
}

effect fn plain() -> i32 {
  return 1
}

effect fn traced() -> i32 ? &Tracer {
  return run Tracer.trace(1)
}

effect fn measure() -> i32 ? &Option<&Tracer> {
  return run withSome<&Tracer>(plain(), traced())
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let offset = Offset {amount: 10}
  let none = Option<never>.none()
  let present = run provideSome<&Tracer>(measure(), &offset)
  let absent = run Effect.provide(measure(), &none)
  if present != 11 || absent != 1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Option"></a>

## `Option`

```silk
pub union Option<T>
```

An owned value of type `T` that is present ([`Some`](#Option.Some)) or absent ([`None`](#Option.None)).

### When to use

Use `Option` as a return type when "no value" is a normal result and needs no reason. Use
`silk.result.Result` when the caller must know why the value is missing.

### Details

Create values with [`some`](#Option.impl.some) and [`none`](#Option.impl.none). Test them with [`isSome`](#Option.impl.isSome) and [`isNone`](#Option.impl.isNone). Use [`map`](#Option.impl.map),
[`flatMap`](#Option.impl.flatMap), and [`unwrapOr`](#Option.impl.unwrapOr) for the common cases. Use `match` when the two cases need
different custom behavior. The option owns its value, so dropping a present option also drops
the value.

In a requirement row, `&Option<&S>` is an optional service: the effect runs with or without a
provider of `S`. Branch on it with [`withSome`](#withSome).

### Examples

#### Handle both cases with `match`

```silk
import silk.option { Option }

fn describe(found: Option<i32>) -> i32 {
  return match move found {
    Option<i32>.Some { value } => value
    Option<i32>.None => -1
  }
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let found = describe(Option<i32>.some(3))
  let missing = describe(Option<i32>.none())
  if found != 3 || missing != -1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Option.impl.none"></a>

### Associated function `none`

```silk
pub fn none() -> Option<T>
```

Returns an absent `Option<T>`.

#### Details

The result holds no value and allocates no memory. Write the element type explicitly, as in
`Option<i32>.none()`, because no argument gives the compiler that type.

<a id="Option.impl.some"></a>

### Associated function `some`

```silk
pub fn some(value: T) -> Option<T>
```

Returns a present `Option<T>` that owns `value`.

#### Details

This function moves `value` into the option. The caller can no longer use the original
binding.

<a id="Option.impl.isSome"></a>

### Method `isSome`

```silk
pub fn isSome(self: &Self) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `self` holds a value.

#### When to use

Use `isSome` when only the presence matters. Use `match` or [`unwrapOr`](#Option.impl.unwrapOr) to read the value.

#### Details

This function borrows `self`, so the option and its value stay available.

#### Examples

##### Test an option and keep it

```silk
import silk.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let found = Option<i32>.some(3)
  if !Option<i32>.isSome(&found) {
    return 1
  }
  let value = move found |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  return value - 3
}
```

<a id="Option.impl.isNone"></a>

### Method `isNone`

```silk
pub fn isNone(self: &Self) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `self` holds no value.

#### When to use

Use `isNone` when only the absence matters, such as to stop a search early. Use `match` or
[`unwrapOr`](#Option.impl.unwrapOr) to read a present value.

#### Details

This function borrows `self`, so the option and its value stay available.

#### Examples

##### Test an absent option

```silk
import silk.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let missing = Option<i32>.none()
  if !Option<i32>.isNone(&missing) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Option.impl.map"></a>

### Method `map`

```silk
pub fn map<U>(self: Self, transform: once fn(T) -> U) -> Option<U>
```

Returns `transform(value)` as a present option if `self` is present. Returns an absent option
if `self` is absent.

#### When to use

Use `map` when the transform always succeeds. Use [`flatMap`](#Option.impl.flatMap) when the transform can also
produce no value.

#### Details

`transform` runs one time for a present value and does not run for an absent value. This
function consumes `self` and moves the present value into `transform`.

#### Gotchas

The original option is not available after the call. To read the value and keep the option,
use `match` on a borrow of the option.

#### Examples

##### Double a present value

```silk
import silk.option { Option }

fn double(value: i32) -> i32 {
  return value * 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let doubled = Option<i32>.some(21) |> Option<i32>.map<i32>(double) |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  if doubled != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Option.impl.flatMap"></a>

### Method `flatMap`

```silk
pub fn flatMap<U>(self: Self, transform: once fn(T) -> Option<U>) -> Option<U>
```

Returns the option that `transform` produces for a present value. Returns an absent option if
`self` is absent.

#### When to use

Use `flatMap` to chain steps where each step can produce no value. The result is one
`Option<U>`, not a nested `Option<Option<U>>`. Use [`map`](#Option.impl.map) when the step always produces a
value.

#### Details

`transform` runs one time for a present value and does not run for an absent value. This
function consumes `self` and moves the present value into `transform`.

#### Examples

##### Reject a value in the second step

```silk
import silk.option { Option }

fn positive(value: i32) -> Option<i32> {
  if value > 0 {
    return Option<i32>.some(value)
  }
  return Option<i32>.none()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let kept = Option<i32>.some(5) |> Option<i32>.flatMap<i32>(positive) |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  let rejected = Option<i32>.some(-5) |> Option<i32>.flatMap<i32>(positive)
    |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  if kept != 5 || rejected != 0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Option.impl.unwrapOr"></a>

### Method `unwrapOr`

```silk
pub fn unwrapOr(
    self: Self,
    /// The value to return if `self` is absent. It is dropped if `self` is present.
    fallback: T,
  ) -> T
```

Returns the present value. Returns `fallback` if `self` is absent.

#### When to use

Use `unwrapOr` at the end of an option chain when a default value is correct for the absent
case. Use `match` when the absent case needs different control flow, such as an early return.

#### Details

This function consumes `self` and `fallback`. It returns one of the two values and drops the
other value.

#### Gotchas

The caller evaluates `fallback` before the call, also when `self` is present. If the fallback
is expensive to make, use `match` and make the fallback only in the absent case.

#### Examples

##### Use a present value and an absent value

```silk
import silk.option { Option }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let present = Option<i32>.some(7)
  let absent = Option<i32>.none()
  let first = move present |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  let second = move absent |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(5)
  if first != 7 || second != 5 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Option.impl.unwrapOr.fallback"></a>

#### Parameter `fallback`

```silk
fallback: T
```

The value to return if `self` is absent. It is dropped if `self` is present.

<a id="OptionService"></a>

## `OptionService`

```silk
pub service OptionService<?S>
```

The service that an `&Option<&S>` requirement names.

### When to use

Do not name this service in your code. Write `? &Option<&S>` in a requirement row and branch
with [`withSome`](#withSome). Diagnostics name this service where they name the key.

### Details

`Option<&S>` is an ordinary requirement key, separate from `S`. An `Option<P>` provides it when
`&P` provides `S`: `Option<P>.some(provider)` is present and `Option<P>.None` is absent. The
explicit absent provider is `Option<never>.none()`, because `never` serves every service and has
no values. [`provideSome`](#provideSome) lifts a borrowed provider of `S` into a present one.

<a id="OptionService.select"></a>

### Operation `select`

```silk
effect<'env> fn select<'env, A, E, ?R>(
    absent: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    present: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R | S>,
  ) -> A ! E ? R | &OptionService<S>
  where R in Without<R, S>
```

Runs `present` with the provider of `S` when one exists, otherwise runs `absent`.

<a id="withSome"></a>

## `withSome`

```silk
pub effect fn withSome<'env, ?S, A, E, ?R>(
  absent: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
  present: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R | S>,
) -> A ! E ? R | &OptionService<S>
where R in Without<R, S>
```

Runs `present` when the optional service `S` has a provider, otherwise runs `absent`.

### When to use

Use this function inside an effect that requires `&Option<&S>`, where the work differs with
and without `S`, for example optional tracing or metrics.

### Details

The type argument is the requirement entry, such as `withSome<&Tracer>`. The provider decides
the branch at runtime with one tag check. The branch that does not run is dropped. Both branches
share the other requirements `R`, which must not contain `S`, and only `present` may use `S`.

### Gotchas

A provider of `S` does not satisfy `&Option<&S>`. Provide `Option<P>.some(provider)`,
`Option<never>.none()`, or use [`provideSome`](#provideSome).

<a id="Present"></a>

## `Present`

```silk
pub struct Present<'env, P>
```

A borrowed provider that always serves an optional service as present.

### Details

[`provideSome`](#provideSome) makes one for a single provision. Use `Option<P>` instead when the provider is
owned or when presence is decided at runtime.

effect<'run> fn select<'run, A, E, ?R>(

<a id="provideSome"></a>

## `provideSome`

```silk
pub effect fn provideSome<'env, ?S, A, P, E, ?R>(
  program: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
  provider: &'env P,
) -> A ! E ? Without<R, OptionService<S>>
where &Present<'env, P> provides OptionService<S> from R
```

Provides a borrowed provider of `S` to the optional requirement `&Option<S>` of `program`.

### When to use

Use this function when you have a provider of `S` and the effect requires `&Option<S>`. A
provider of `S` does not satisfy `&Option<S>` without this explicit lift.

### Details

The type argument is the requirement entry, such as `provideSome<&Tracer>`. The provider stays
borrowed for the execution of `program`. Every other requirement in `R` stays visible in the
result.
